label: EN-欧盟
paragraphs: EU NEV, Battery & CBAM Policy Timeline (2010–2026.04)
Based on government public information. Items marked [needs verification] should be cross-checked with original documents.
tables: Directive 2009/33/EC on the promotion of clean and energy-efficient road transport vehicles (Clean Vehicles Directive)
Public procurement must account for lifetime energy consumption and CO₂/pollutant emissions; promotes clean vehicles in public fleets
Part of European Economic Recovery Plan (~€5bn); supports automotive R&D in low-carbon tech including batteries and electric powertrains
Promotes EV-smart grid integration; unified charging standard framework; supports V2G technology
European Commission, Smart Grids Task Force
Proposes alternative fuels infrastructure (charging, LNG, hydrogen); lays foundation for 2014 AFID
Directive 2014/94/EU on the deployment of alternative fuels infrastructure (AFID)
Member states must develop National Policy Frameworks (NPFs) for charging/hydrogen coverage; unified Type 2/CCS charging standard
Five dimensions: energy security, internal market, energy efficiency, decarbonisation, R&D; identifies EVs as key transport decarbonisation pathway
Accelerates ZEV deployment, unified charging infrastructure market, alternative fuels and digital transport applications
Approves Important Projects of Common European Interest (IPCEI) in battery value chain; permits state aid for battery R&D and production
VP Šefčovič launched EBA with Member States, industry and research; goal: build autonomous EU battery manufacturing. EU had ~3% of global cell capacity
Six priority areas covering full value chain (raw materials, manufacturing, recycling, tech, skills, regulation); target: build complete EU battery industry
Regulation (EU) 2019/631 — CO₂ emission performance standards for new passenger cars and light commercial vehicles
2025 targets (cars 95g/km, vans 147g/km); 2030 reduction -37.5% (cars) / -31% (vans); ZLEV super-credit mechanism
Regulation (EU) 2019/1242 — CO₂ emission performance standards for new heavy-duty vehicles
First EU-wide HDV CO₂ standards; covers HD lorries >16t (~70% HDV CO₂); 2025 target: -15%
Foundational strategy: climate neutrality by 2050; 2030 net GHG ≥ -55% (vs 1990); drives clean mobility, circular economy, energy transition; commits to revising all climate/energy legislation
Includes Battery Regulation proposal, sustainable product legislation, critical raw materials circularity; emphasizes battery circularity and sustainability
Lists Li, Co, graphite, rare earths as critical; action plan to reduce single-supplier dependency
Transport 90% emission cut by 2050 (vs 1990); milestones: ≥30M ZEVs on road by 2030, 100 climate-neutral cities; 82 initiatives
12 Member States, €2.9bn public funding, full battery value chain coverage
2050 climate neutrality legally binding; 2030 net GHG ≥ -55% (vs 1990); mandates consecutive 2030/2040/2050 targets
Largest climate legislative package (15 proposals). Core: EU ETS reform, CBAM, car CO₂ standards revision (2035 zero-emission), AFIR, RED, EE Directive, Social Climate Fund
CBAM Proposal — Regulation establishing a carbon border adjustment mechanism

Charges on embedded carbon in imports (cement, iron/steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen); price = EU ETS carbon price; transition from 2023, definitive from 2026; linked to EU ETS free allowance phase-out
European Parliament votes to ban new ICE cars/vans from 2035
Votes: 2035 onwards newly registered cars/vans must have zero CO₂ (de facto ICE ban including sedans/SUVs/vans); Commission to review progress by 2026 considering technology neutrality
Transitional phase 2023.10–2025.12; definitive regime from 2026.01; phased phase-out of EU ETS free allowances; sectors: cement, steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen
Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) Provisional Agreement
Targets: EV fast charger every 60km on TEN-T by 2026; truck charger every 120km by 2028; hydrogen station every 200km by 2031; unified payment
Green Deal Industrial Plan / Net-Zero Industry Act Proposal

Response to US IRA; includes NZIA, CRMA, electricity market reform; target: EU domestic net-zero tech manufacturing ≥40% of annual deployment needs by 2030; batteries listed as strategic net-zero technology
2030 benchmarks: strategic RM extraction 10%, processing 40%, recycling 25% from within EU; single-country dependency ≤65% at any processing stage; simplified permitting
Regulation (EU) 2023/851 — Amending CO₂ standards for cars and vans (formally adopted)
Formal adoption: 2030 -55% cars, -50% vans; 2035 zero CO₂ for new vehicles (de facto ICE ban); Commission to review technology neutrality (including e-fuels) by 2026

World's first full life-cycle battery regulation: carbon footprint declaration/class/threshold, recycled content, Battery Passport, supply chain due diligence, collection targets; phased from 2024; Battery Passport from 2027
Effective; carbon footprint label from 2025; class from 2026; threshold + Battery Passport from 2027; mandatory recycled content from 2030 (Co 16%, Pb 85%, Li 6%, Ni 6%)
Transitional phase 2023.10–2025.12; importers must report embedded emissions quarterly; no financial payment required
Regulation (EU) 2023/1804 — Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) formally adopted
AFID upgraded to binding Regulation, replacing Directive 2014/94/EU
Unified emission rules for cars, vans, trucks, buses; first to regulate brake/tyre particle emissions and battery durability
Regulation (EU) 2024/1610 — HDV CO₂ emission standards revised
Extended scope (medium/heavy trucks, buses, coaches, trailers); new targets: 2030 -45%, 2035 -65%, 2040 -90%; new city buses 90% ZEV from 2030, 100% from 2035
EU imposes additional tariffs on Chinese BEVs
Anti-subsidy investigation results: additional tariffs on Chinese BEVs: BYD 17.0%, Geely 18.8%, SAIC 35.3% (on top of 10% base tariff)
Critical Raw Materials Act enters into force — Regulation (EU) 2024/1252
Effective; 17 strategic and 34 critical raw materials lists
Net-Zero Industry Act enters into force — Regulation (EU) 2025/703

Batteries listed as strategic net-zero technology; mandatory non-price criteria (sustainability, resilience) in procurement/auctions; target ≥40% EU manufacturing by 2030; Net-Zero Acceleration Valleys
Minimum Import Price (MIP) mechanism partially replaces anti-subsidy tariffs; China withdraws WTO case [needs verification of specific terms]

Three pillars: ① Revised CO₂ standards — 90% tailpipe zero-emission from 2035, remaining 10% offsetable via low-carbon steel, e-fuels, or biofuels; ② Battery Booster (€1.8bn for battery manufacturing); ③ Automotive Omnibus (regulatory simplification, ~€706m/year savings)
CO₂ Standards Review — 2035 ICE ban flexibility adjustments
Maintains 2035 direction but adds compliance flexibility (e-fuels, biofuels, low-carbon material offsets) based on review obligation under Reg 2023/851 Art.15

Imports >50t/year threshold must apply for authorised CBAM declarant status; purchase CBAM certificates (priced at quarterly avg of EU ETS auction price; weekly avg from 2027); annual declaration and surrender; carbon price paid abroad deductible
Battery carbon footprint labelling enters into effect
Batteries Regulation Art.7 implementation — mandatory A-E carbon footprint label for all EV batteries placed on EU market
European Climate Law amended — 2040 target set
New legally binding 2040 target: net GHG -90% vs 1990 (domestic -85%, int'l carbon credits ≤5%)
First CBAM certificate quarterly price published based on EU ETS auction price; ~€89/tCO₂ [needs verification of exact figure]
